dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC CROWN RING — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: I can see her table through the door. That's my mother's table. Whoever told you this apartment was vacant didn't bother opening it.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: The placement office gave us a key. We arrived after midnight. We thought—

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: I know exactly what you thought. Everybody's been telling me what they thought since I got here.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: We can move our things.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: And sleep where? You almost passed out walking over.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I can sleep sitting up. I've had practice.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: So has my mother. That's rather the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Your mother keeps this apartment. The emergency placement is temporary. Nobody is being thrown into the concourse this morning.

panelPlan: AURIC CROWN RING — MORNING. The polished concourse has a view worth a year's rent. An elderly woman is waiting outside her own apartment, short of breath.
Halev and Sera Dain arrive with a clerk carrying two contradictory housing allocations. Halev accepts both papers; Sera takes them out of his hands before he.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC CROWN RING — MORNING. The polished concourse has a view worth a year's rent. An elderly woman is waiting outside her own apartment, short of breath, while her daughter argues with a placement clerk. Inside are Richard Secundo, Paul, and the belongings of an exhausted refugee family.*
*Halev and Sera Dain arrive with a clerk carrying two contradictory housing allocations. Halev accepts both papers; Sera takes them out of his hands before he can make promises.*

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: That is three families you've just fitted inside one sentence. How many beds do you think we have?

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Two, by the inspection. The third is a chair that someone has called a bed because it doesn't have an armrest.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I can find another room.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: You can ask. Those are different verbs.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: May I listen to your breathing?

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: She's not a prop in a housing negotiation.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Neither am I. May I?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Dad. Heat's out.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: It was working when we left.

panelPlan: The elderly woman coughs. Richard turns away from the argument and goes to her.
The daughter nods. Richard crouches beside the older woman. Inside, the heater ticks, attempts to start, and stops.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The elderly woman coughs. Richard turns away from the argument and goes to her.*
*The daughter nods. Richard crouches beside the older woman. Inside, the heater ticks, attempts to start, and stops.*

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I'll send engineering.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You said that about the lock yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Then today you'll get the same engineer twice. It's the most economical arrangement we have.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: Aren't those for your people?

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: At the moment, your mother is my people. Help me sit her up.

panelPlan: Richard opens a precious medical kit. The daughter notices the few remaining doses.
Later, in the corridor, Sera has drawn a route to a warmer room; there are no spare beds there either. The daughter takes her mother's hand. Paul lifts their.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Richard opens a precious medical kit. The daughter notices the few remaining doses.*

*Later, in the corridor, Sera has drawn a route to a warmer room; there are no spare beds there either. The daughter takes her mother's hand. Paul lifts their bag rather than ask anyone to choose who carries what. For once, no one discusses legal entitlement.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You're going back to the people who took your ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: They ordered me to appear.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Very persuasive people, the Admiralty.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You know I couldn't ignore the summons.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I know you can ignore an order when you're convinced it's wrong. We've established that.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I gave the rescue order. I'll explain it myself. My crew shouldn't have to guess whether I intend to stand behind them.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: They'll ask how many passengers you saved. You'll tell them. Someone will mention the heaters that never arrived; you'll tell them that too. Then the doors open and a transport carries you someplace warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You're angry.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That's observant.

panelPlan: AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS. The damaged Thunderbreak is no longer Venn's command. She watches workers struggle to move a heater cart through a too-narrow.
Venn finally looks at her.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS. The damaged Thunderbreak is no longer Venn's command. She watches workers struggle to move a heater cart through a too-narrow service door. Naomi Sol approaches, hair still damp from a rushed wash.*
*Venn finally looks at her.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I don't know what you want me to say.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I want you to look at the place you're leaving. Not at the window. At the people trying to fit a heater through a door that was built for freight.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I thought the rescue was the difficult decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: It was. It wasn't the last one.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: The supply convoy carried heat and medicine for thousands. Did you know that when you turned Thunderbreak?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: And when you refused to separate the Shard patients, you understood that the detention order came from this command?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I did.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You seem determined to answer the easy questions.

panelPlan: Venn watches the crew rotate the cart, fail, then remove its side panel and try again.
On Dawnward Horizon, Dominion runs the hearing without relish. Admiral Keating reads the assigned convoy protection order; Kerr watches Venn's hands rather.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn watches the crew rotate the cart, fail, then remove its side panel and try again.*
*On Dawnward Horizon, Dominion runs the hearing without relish. Admiral Keating reads the assigned convoy protection order; Kerr watches Venn's hands rather than the record.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You've asked them twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I'm trying to understand what happens the next time someone on a damaged civilian hull asks for help while your assigned convoy is at risk. What should a captain do?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I can tell you what I did. I can't tell you it would be safe to do it every time.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: That is not a reassuring command philosophy.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't trying to reassure you.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: The people in Auric need a military that can keep a promise. The freighters we did not protect had people waiting for their cargo, too. I won't let those families disappear because you can see a distressed ship on a screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Neither will I.

panelPlan: Venn hesitates, not for effect.
During recess, Kerr intercepts her with a revised defense.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn hesitates, not for effect.*
*During recess, Kerr intercepts her with a revised defense.*

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: If you say you protected Fleet's strategic standing at Auric, this may survive. It isn't even false. Auric might have turned against us if we'd abandoned those passengers.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: That wasn't my reason.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: People don't ordinarily insist on damaging themselves this thoroughly.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It would be a rather obvious lie. I'd have to pretend I made a calculation I didn't have time to make.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: You're allowed to be right for the wrong reason, Ella.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then let the record say what the reason was. If they dismiss me for it, at least there won't be two versions of me walking around Fleet headquarters.

panelPlan: Kerr studies her and removes the rewritten statement from the table. For the first time, he has nothing useful to add.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Kerr studies her and removes the rewritten statement from the table. For the first time, he has nothing useful to add.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — IMPROVISED CLINIC

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: These patients came from three districts. Why do they all look like they've spent the winter in the same broken room?

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: They were deprived of the same power system.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Officially, three unrelated failures.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's unfortunate. The machines must have been conspiring.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You can see the command entries here. Somebody replaced the original log.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I was on a supply run the month these dates start. They told us the shutoffs were emergency load management. We carried spare parts to the wrong side of the line and went home.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: If you'd known?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. That's a question people ask when they're trying to make themselves feel better about what they didn't do.

panelPlan: An improvised clinic has been installed in an Auric apartment. Richard has laid printed service orders beneath a repaired medical lamp. Paul holds up a second.
Richard spreads out the original distribution orders. The districts lost heat and medicine after protesting Triarch policy. Another district.
Paul opens his mouth, thinks better of it, and resumes sorting.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *An improvised clinic has been installed in an Auric apartment. Richard has laid printed service orders beneath a repaired medical lamp. Paul holds up a second set with different timestamps. Tessa Banks has taken off her coat to work at a pressure regulator.*
*Richard spreads out the original distribution orders. The districts lost heat and medicine after protesting Triarch policy. Another district continued receiving supply.*
*Paul opens his mouth, thinks better of it, and resumes sorting.*

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: The orders are signed. The medical copies were changed twice. Someone intended the patients to be invisible.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: They failed. You've been keeping them alive long enough to annoy their government.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: The room outside's warmer.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Outside has fewer people trying to breathe in it.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Here. Use our blanket.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You don't even know us.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: I know she needs it. I can be introduced afterward.

panelPlan: They are interrupted by the returning resident and her mother, who is wheezing again. A Luminara boy follows his mother into the warming room. The boy looks at.
The older woman laughs once, then coughs. Richard adjusts her position. Tess stops speaking about the records to hold the lamp steady. The evidence can wait.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *They are interrupted by the returning resident and her mother, who is wheezing again. A Luminara boy follows his mother into the warming room. The boy looks at the tiny heater.*
*The older woman laughs once, then coughs. Richard adjusts her position. Tess stops speaking about the records to hold the lamp steady. The evidence can wait for one human body to find its breath.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — CIVIC CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: The next section is closed. The heaters are not holding.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We can't leave people in the concourse.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We can lease private apartments. The owners will insist on a security deposit, and before anyone looks at me that way, those are people who paid for rooms they haven't been able to use themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You can lease a thousand beautiful cold apartments. We'll still have a thousand cold families.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Well, if you have warm apartments I've neglected to mention, Captain, this is a marvelous time to produce them.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Stop. You can both win later. I have twenty-three rooms we can heat safely and more than a hundred people to move.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Can we divert power from freight?

panelPlan: Auric civic chamber. Halev has asked for the number of warmed rooms. Sera has brought a number he doesn't like. Wallace has brought a contract he doesn't like..
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Auric civic chamber. Halev has asked for the number of warmed rooms. Sera has brought a number he doesn't like. Wallace has brought a contract he doesn't like. Naomi has brought a route report nobody wants to read.*

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: For a night, yes. Then the shipments stop. The freight motors aren't decorative.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: They've called back the people who have been keeping the clinic equipment going.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Can Venn stop it?

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Venn doesn't command the ship anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: I don't imagine Dominion enjoys making us cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: That'll be a comfort to the people who are cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Twenty-three rooms. Assign them to the people we can move safely. We tell everyone else what the count is. If a merchant offers us a room with no heat, we take the room, but we do not call it shelter.

panelPlan: A message from Deka arrives. The Admiralty has ordered Thunderbreak beyond Auric's defense boundary; its temporary medical-power detachment is leaving with it.
Halev sees the quarrel hardening into slogans.
Wallace starts reviewing the lease terms. Naomi takes the revised route sheet to dispatch. Nobody has solved the problem, but three people have something real.

summary: THE ROUTE THAT WASN'T ON THE BOARD (P08, P20–P21) — 1/3

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: Three strangers asked for your Auric crossing by name. None had a family aboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: It is possible I have achieved a degree of fame.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: You've been charging strangers for secrets so long you've mistaken their interest for admiration.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I've been providing people a service.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: You provided Billie with a service too.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'll close the public entrance once the last vessels clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: They're following the people who leave it. Those people arrive at my door.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'm aware of the geography.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: Then start behaving as if you care what happens at the other end of it.

panelPlan: Veil Market. Jex is trying to close a public approach without admitting how many people are still using it. His sister Tali stands at a private terminal.
He looks away. Tali refuses to make the accusation twice.
Later, Naomi brings evidence that the public passage is under observation. An evacuation convoy cannot get through it.

summary: THE ROUTE THAT WASN'T ON THE BOARD (P08, P20–P21) — 2/3

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I need another approach. I can cover arrivals. I can't see where the raiders are sitting behind the departure points.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: There's one, but I cannot hand you a map without handing somebody my sister's front door.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: It's my front door. Ask me.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If I send it, the watchers can work backward. Even with the traffic dispersed.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: Then I warn the families, move them off the access, and tell you when. You can complain about the cost afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You think I wouldn't pay it?

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: I think you always make sure you get an invoice. This time I'm writing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: Open it now.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Tali, leave. You've done what you can.

panelPlan: Jex holds her gaze.
She contacts the families. The next civilian vessel is already nearing the ambush.
Jex sends the private timing. Naomi brings the first transports through. Incoming hostile contacts converge on the exposed safehouse.

summary: THE ROUTE THAT WASN'T ON THE BOARD (P08, P20–P21) — 3/3

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: There's one family still at the last access. Give me another minute.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You don't have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TALI
dialogueInline.text: Then stop wasting it talking to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We lost the connection.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Not the person. You haven't shown me that.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: No. I haven't.

panelPlan: The signal disappears. Jex keeps his hand on the control. Naomi has seen too many people disappear from sensors to mistake that for a death certificate.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — CLINIC

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: If he went back, do you think they'd actually leave Auric alone?

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: They want the records. And me.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: That's not what I asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: We know what they did with districts that took their word for it.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: We also know what they'll do to this station if he refuses.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I've been thinking about that since the message arrived.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: You were thinking about going?

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I was thinking about every patient whose life depends on someone continuing to deliver medicine. I don't think they will honor the bargain. I wish I were sure enough to stop thinking about it.

panelPlan: At the clinic, the Trade Mask's public message promises restored commerce and amnesty in exchange for Richard Secundo. Tess listens without speaking. Paul.
Richard does not correct him. Paul is not a child who can be comforted with a promise.
Outside, Abby arrives unarmed through an Auric security lock. Sera watches her hands; Naomi makes no attempt to conceal her distrust.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *At the clinic, the Trade Mask's public message promises restored commerce and amnesty in exchange for Richard Secundo. Tess listens without speaking. Paul leans against the wall, tired enough to look older than nineteen.*
*Richard does not correct him. Paul is not a child who can be comforted with a promise.*
*Outside, Abby arrives unarmed through an Auric security lock. Sera watches her hands; Naomi makes no attempt to conceal her distrust.*

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Your ships remain beyond our defense line.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They are. I left my weapons in your little locker. It took longer to persuade it to accept them than I expected.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Tell us why you're here.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Billie and Pike are gathering captains to take Richard. Six might agree to protect your civilian transports. Maybe fewer when they understand where they'll have to fly.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Why should we trust you?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You shouldn't. Trust the arrangement you can inspect. Your traffic control. Your destinations. Every captain agreeing separately. If we depart from it, you tell us to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: And if we can't make you leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then you have discovered the problem we've spent generations arguing about.

panelPlan: Naomi considers her, then turns the local defense chart toward her.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Naomi considers her, then turns the local defense chart toward her.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Let's begin with the ships that are actually here, not the ones you're hoping will be brave.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Come with me. I can't keep you safe if they arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Nobody's asked you to keep me safe. I'm old enough to know where the doors are.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I grew up being sent to find you whenever you vanished. Some habits stick.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I spent those years commanding a ship. I heard about the shutoffs. I didn't look too closely at who had to go without heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: We weren't the ones giving the orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No. That's what I've been telling myself. It's a comfort, and there's not much of it left.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I don't want to lose you here.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then help Naomi keep those craft clear. And stop trying to make me come home when there are patients on the floor.

panelPlan: Later, Abby finds Tess in a clinic passage.
Abby leaves her a locator token. Tess pockets it without surrendering her post.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — ARCHIVE BOOTH

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: We can show your documents and protect your location on the feed. We can't promise the Triarch won't identify the room afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: They know where I am. They offered to take me back on air.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I'd still like you to live long enough to see whether your testimony makes a difference.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: Dad, you don't have to read every name.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I think I do.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: I meant you don't have to do it alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Nemi Vale. Forty-two. The breathing system in her district lost power the day after the protest. Ors Dane was denied antibiotics when the new consignment was diverted. Sergeant Pell took medicine into a closed district. They called it theft. They executed him for it.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: These aren't anonymous outages. These are orders. Here are the originals. Here is what was changed in the official copies.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BROKEN OATH — WAR ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Secundo's records are already copied. We can't put them back. We can make Auric decide it isn't worth keeping him.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: How?

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Cut the luxury ring's heat exchanger. Leave a medical patch near it. They'll start accusing the people in the clinic. We collect Secundo while security is trying to keep residents from fighting one another.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You could kill someone doing that.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: If we move quickly, we won't have to.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: That's what you say when you haven't bothered counting.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: You've asked me to get the doctor. I'm telling you how.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Away from the clinic. Secundo comes out breathing. No firing into the patients.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

panelPlan: Broken Oath's war room. Pike has arranged the attack as neatly as he arranges his broadcasts. Billie listens with the expression of someone trying to convince.
He has heard the restriction. It has not changed his plan enough.
The exchanger is cut. A resident finds the patch and begins shouting. In the crowd, Paul tries to prevent someone from knocking down a woman with a child.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Broken Oath's war room. Pike has arranged the attack as neatly as he arranges his broadcasts. Billie listens with the expression of someone trying to convince herself that a bad idea is merely unpleasant.*
*She stares at the station's schematic.*

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: That thing was next to the broken heat unit. It's like the doctor's equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: It's a patch. There are thousands of them in every supply hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: He came here and now our heat is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: No one's leaving until we get the patients clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: The exchanger was cut by hand. That's sabotage.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: So arrest the person who did it.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I don't know who did it. Neither do you. A patch isn't a confession.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: People already know the heat's failing. They're moving blind.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: We tell them which rooms still have working systems, and which doors are actually open. We tell them what we cannot promise.

panelPlan: Sera arrives with Halev and Naomi. The crowd wants certainty, not maintenance instructions.
At civic control, Halev hesitates before authorizing a warning that may produce panic.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Sera arrives with Halev and Naomi. The crowd wants certainty, not maintenance instructions.*
*At civic control, Halev hesitates before authorizing a warning that may produce panic.*

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: If they rush the inner shelter—

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then give them a route instead of giving them a rumor.

dialogueInline.speaker: GUARD
dialogueInline.text: Your order says registered residents first. They're not registered.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then my order is wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: GUARD
dialogueInline.text: Governor, my instructions—

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I know. I signed them. Let them through. Write down that I corrected it, and if someone wants to remove me for it they can get in line behind the heater engineers.

panelPlan: They broadcast the real instructions. At the inner shelter a guard refuses the refugees under a residency rule Halev himself signed.
Sera offers her family's berth, a concrete loss she is not eager to romanticize. The people move again.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

*Sera offers her family's berth, a concrete loss she is not eager to romanticize. The people move again.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — LUXURY RING SERVICE CORRIDOR

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Secundo comes out alive. Tell the boarding crews twice, since once doesn't seem to last.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: We're already losing our window.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then make it count.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You said there could be more.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: There could have been. Six said yes. The rest are deciding whether they want to be called traitors tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: My pilots coordinate the civilian lane. Your ships hold the outer cover. Don't chase anyone who pulls away.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: That's the deal I brought them.

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: We can't outrun those ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You don't have to. Keep your bow on the route. My people are coming between you and the guns.

panelPlan: Attack craft dock to the service side of Auric's luxury ring. A pressure corridor rattles under impact. Billie moves toward Richard's clinic; Pike stays with.
The six Shard craft intercept fire intended for unarmed transports. Naomi directs vessels off the exposed approach.
On Thunderbreak, acting commander Erin Deka sees the same attacks from beyond Auric's defense boundary.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Attack craft dock to the service side of Auric's luxury ring. A pressure corridor rattles under impact. Billie moves toward Richard's clinic; Pike stays with his projected line of retreat.*

*The six Shard craft intercept fire intended for unarmed transports. Naomi directs vessels off the exposed approach.*

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Admiralty has not released us to cross.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I can read the order. Put the civilian hulls on the main display.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: That won't change what it says.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: No. It will change what we can honestly say we saw.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You can return to command if you support a managed withdrawal. Secundo comes under Fleet protection; Auric stops being the battlefield for this evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You mean custody.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I mean a living witness. This is not a philosophical distinction to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It isn't to Secundo either. He's told us he will not go into Fleet detention. What authority does Auric have if we solve every dangerous civilian problem by taking the civilian away?

panelPlan: At the tribunal, Dominion offers Venn a path back to Thunderbreak in exchange for accepting controlled withdrawal and civilian witness custody.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *At the tribunal, Dominion offers Venn a path back to Thunderbreak in exchange for accepting controlled withdrawal and civilian witness custody.*

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You've spent this hearing refusing to distinguish your convictions from your authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know exactly where my authority ends. I don't command Thunderbreak now.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: We can see transports being hit. I want you to know what we're looking at.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: My suspension stands. I can't tell you where to take your ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: No, Commodore. You can't.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Helm. Take us across the boundary. Bring our armored side between those ships and the clinic approach. If someone wants my explanation later, tell them I'll have a very good view.

panelPlan: Deka's communication opens. The captain hears the exchange but receives no order from Venn.
Deka looks back at her crew.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — CLINIC CORRIDOR

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You're really going to stand there.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I've been standing here all day. It's a dreadful position. There are better places to make an argument.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Come with me. Secundo has to answer for what he published.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: He published the records. Taking him won't put the words back in his mouth.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Abby's made me an enemy. You didn't even tell me you'd chosen her.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I didn't choose her. I chose this corridor. There are people at the other end who can't walk.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You were my family before these people ever knew your name.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You still are. I hate that I have to tell you to stop frightening them.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You think I enjoy this?

panelPlan: The clinic corridor is full of patients being moved in improvised restraints. Tess stands in its narrowest point. Billie comes around the damaged bulkhead and.
Tess is silent. That one reaches her.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The clinic corridor is full of patients being moved in improvised restraints. Tess stands in its narrowest point. Billie comes around the damaged bulkhead and stops when she sees her.*
*Tess is silent. That one reaches her.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I think you've got very good at making yourself angry enough not to notice.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Doctor, you'd be safer letting me bleed.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: Probably. Paul, hold this dressing. Tessa, is that inner door secure?

dialogueInline.speaker: PAUL
dialogueInline.text: She's the one who came for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: RICHARD
dialogueInline.text: I remember. Press harder.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Pike's gone. You can come with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You think carrying me out makes this all right?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: No. I think you should be alive for the part where we all decide what to do with you.

panelPlan: The breach shakes. Billie steps toward Tess; Tess does not move. A stray impact wounds Billie during the retreat. Pike's craft depart without waiting for her..
Abby appears at the opposite end.
Billie refuses the hand. Richard continues working. No one calls it reconciliation.

*Abby appears at the opposite end.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — DAMAGED RING

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: We can hold the heated inner rooms tonight. Tomorrow we lose another section unless we get the exchanger rebuilt.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: What if we offer residency to the families who've come here? Not a promise that we have homes ready. A right to stay while we build them.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: You'll be asking people with contracts to finance an arrangement they voted against.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: I thought you might at least hesitate.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I have. For three days. That's been long enough to get everyone angry with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The defense agreement stays civilian. Shard captains can volunteer, but Auric directs traffic and rescue. No permanent Fleet base arrives inside a paragraph nobody read.

panelPlan: After the attack, emergency crews seal damaged ring compartments. Patients still need beds. More Shard captains have helped defend civilian craft, and their.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *After the attack, emergency crews seal damaged ring compartments. Patients still need beds. More Shard captains have helped defend civilian craft, and their crews are now distrusted by the people they saved.*

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: My captains decide individually. Nobody's joining an army because I liked the look of this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: And we still have ships to fix. It would help if we stopped shooting the docks we're trying to use.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We have contacts watching the safehouse approaches. None has seen her.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That's not the same as seeing she didn't get out.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I've always been able to buy someone who knew which way to look. Now they're all asking me for information I don't have.

panelPlan: At Veil Market, Jex waits beside Tali's silent token. Halev calls with the offer of help.
He closes the call before he says something cruel to a man who has tried to help.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *At Veil Market, Jex waits beside Tali's silent token. Halev calls with the offer of help.*
*He closes the call before he says something cruel to a man who has tried to help.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FLEET TRANSIT COMPARTMENT

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Auric voted for residency. It means some families will stay in freight halls a month from now, but at least nobody can send them away because their permit is late.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: That's more than we gave them.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You sound surprised.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I am. I spent a lifetime believing that if Fleet could reopen the roads, the rest would follow. I never had to calculate the number of beds at the end of one.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: When you left, I was angry. Then I got angrier because I wondered if you were glad to be leaving.

panelPlan: Venn is leaving under Fleet disciplinary orders. Naomi finds her at the transit compartment. Through the port, Auric's beautiful rings are still half repaired.
Venn looks through the glass for some time.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn is leaving under Fleet disciplinary orders. Naomi finds her at the transit compartment. Through the port, Auric's beautiful rings are still half repaired and crowded with people.*
*Venn looks through the glass for some time.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: There were mornings I was grateful to have a clear order. The kind that could be completed, logged, and handed to someone else. It's an ugly thing to admit while you were still moving people out of the cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You could have told me.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I should have.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: So what happens now?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'm being sent away without Thunderbreak. That much is settled. Beyond that, I intend to find a way to come back useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then bring something we can use. Not a speech about the importance of connection.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You've heard that one?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Every Fleet officer who ever needed a docking bay has delivered it to me.

panelPlan: Venn lets herself smile, briefly.
The transit hatch closes. Neither woman has forgiven the other for what she cannot fix. Both know what the next conversation will have to concern.
